modes.label: Credit-metered browser session
modes.note: 30-second increments documented but current credits per time/CPU/token/GB conversion not disclosed. Browser runs server-side (Linux); os set to linux so the regime is considered. features.ip_note: Integrated residential proxy (US default, ~10-min sticky IPs, billed on bandwidth; Starter plan+) or custom proxy (Professional plan+); default non-proxied egress type and per-GB price not published.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Do not divide monthly fee by credits and invent a browser-hour price: browser/AI/proxy credit consumption is not publicly defined in reviewed current docs.
Free signup bonus conflict: marketing 10,000 vs billing guide 30,000 (31,000 initial total), first-cycle only. Annual credit timing also conflicts; preserve both.

Default idle termination 10 minutes; changing timeout is documented. Persistent profiles preserve cookies/local storage, not arbitrary VM RAM. Integrated residential proxy and CAPTCHA features are not evidence that traffic is unmetered.

fleet.tiers: Free and Starter 3 simultaneous sessions; Professional 30; Enterprise 100; Custom negotiated.
fleet.notes: Number of deployed agents is separate from sessions. Buying larger Starter credit bundles does not increase its 3 slots; 10 requires Professional, 50 Enterprise, 300/1,000 Custom.

snapshot_auto.quote: By default, sessions have an idle timeout of 10 minutes. After 10 minutes of inactivity, the session will be automatically terminated.
snapshot_auto.note: Idle/timeout ends the session; nothing is saved unless you called saveProfileOnTermination beforehand ('Profiles are only saved when the sesssion is terminated. You must remember to call sessions.terminate'). Profiles hold cookies + local storage only, no memory/process state.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Profiles are saved archives of the artifacts produced by a browsing session. Most importantly, they contain the cookies and local storage of a session, which can be used to hydrate future sessions and keep the same authenticated state.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No machine/browser snapshot API. The closest analogue is a named browser profile (cookies + local storage), saved only at session termination, which can seed any number of new sessions (profileName). No memory/tab state.

own_agent_api.quote: Triggers an agent execution via webhook. You can optionally provide configuration variables and a callback URL.
own_agent_api.note: Only Airtop's own no-code 'Airtop Agents' (built/deployed in the portal): POST /api/hooks/agents/{agentId}/webhooks/{webhookId}, then GET .../invocations/{invocationId}/result ('Retrieves the status and result of a specific agent invocation'). Runs a pre-deployed agent with variables, not an arbitrary prompt; no event streaming or follow-ups documented; no Claude Code/Codex/etc. Separate Sessions API also has natural-language window automations (create/execute-automation, page-query, prompt-content).

guest_firewall.note: No shell/exec access: API surface is browser-only (sessions, windows, CDP, files, profiles). Each browser runs on its own VM per help docs, but the user cannot run commands in it.

secret_proxy.quote: Once you've logged in, the profile will store all necessary cookies and reuse them when the agent runs in the background, so you don't have to log in every time.
secret_proxy.note: Credentials are cookies/local storage loaded into the browser (profiles, AES-256 at rest), plus OAuth API integrations for Airtop Agents; no credential-injecting outbound proxy with placeholders documented. Custom proxy credentials are passed in session config.

docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; the exposed surface is a browser automation API, not a general-purpose compute machine

nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope, no shell/VM access is exposed to customers

desktop.quote: How to provide interactive access of your browser to your users
desktop.note: not offered: Airtop exposes a live view of the browser window itself (embeddable iframe/CDP), not a full graphical OS desktop with VNC/RDP

anti_bot.quote: Some websites have mechanisms to detect and block bot traffic coming from datacenter IPs. Residential proxies are networks of residential IP addresses that proxy requests, making them look like regular human traffic. Airtop has support for using residential proxies to avoid detection.
anti_bot.note: Integrated residential proxy plus browser fingerprint handling explicitly marketed to defeat anti-bot detection

ssh.quote: Airtop is a cloud browser platform that allows you, your AI Agent, or your automation tools to control a web browser in the cloud.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; only a browser-control REST/SDK API is exposed, no shell/SSH access to the underlying VM

snapshot.quote: Profiles are saved archives of the artifacts produced by a browsing session. Most importantly, they contain the cookies and local storage of a session, which can be used to hydrate future sessions and keep the same authenticated state.
snapshot.note: No disk or memory snapshot of the machine/browser process; the closest analogue (Profiles) is cookies + local storage only, saved at session termination, not a filesystem or memory snapshot.

fork.quote: Profiles are saved archives of the artifacts produced by a browsing session.
fork.note: not offered: a saved Profile can seed new sessions with the same cookies, but that is not cloning a running/stopped machine into new machines

fork_running.quote: A session represents an instance of a browser. Each session is identified by a unique UUID and can contain multiple windows that each can load a page.
fork_running.note: not offered: no API to clone a live running session into a new one

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Profiles are saved archives of the artifacts produced by a browsing session.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: no memory-state clone capability exists

pause_resume.quote: By default, sessions have an idle timeout of 10 minutes. After 10 minutes of inactivity, the session will be automatically terminated.
pause_resume.note: Sessions terminate on idle/timeout rather than pausing; no pause/resume API documented

wake_on_request.quote: A session might be `ended` if it terminated due to idle timeout, if you explicitly terminate it, or if it was terminated due to an error.
wake_on_request.note: Ended sessions are gone; a new session must be created (optionally hydrated from a saved Profile), there is no automatic wake of a stopped session on inbound request

persistent_disk.quote: Profiles are saved archives of the artifacts produced by a browsing session. Most importantly, they contain the cookies and local storage of a session
persistent_disk.note: not offered: only cookies/local-storage Profiles persist across sessions; no general persistent filesystem/disk

volume_attach.quote: Airtop allows your agents to download files from the web. ... you can request that the file being downloaded be written to the local file system.
volume_attach.note: not offered: downloaded files are streamed to the caller's local machine/signed URL, not stored on an attachable provider volume

volume_shared.quote: Airtop is a cloud browser platform that allows you, your AI Agent, or your automation tools to control a web browser in the cloud.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope, no shared-volume concept exists

live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no CPU/RAM sizing knobs for a running session are documented

agent_harnesses.quote: Airtop researches your company, creates a custom plan, and builds AI Agents that automate your entire funnel
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Airtop's 'Connections' page lists Claude Code and Codex as tools that call INTO Airtop (Airtop as an MCP/API tool for those coding harnesses), not coding-agent harnesses preinstalled inside Airtop's own sandboxes.

harness_api.quote: Airtop researches your company, creates a custom plan, and builds AI Agents that automate your entire funnel
harness_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Airtop drives its own browser/task agents (own_agent_api=true), not a third-party coding harness

mcp_server.quote: For AI client integration (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.), connect to the MCP server at https://docs.airtop.ai/_mcp/server
mcp_server.note: Airtop ships an MCP server endpoint for AI clients; used both for docs and, per the pricing page's Claude Code/Codex 'Connections', for driving Airtop sessions from coding agents.

public_ipv4.quote: By default, Airtop-provided proxies will be in the US and will attempt to keep the same IP address 10 minutes.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; sessions are reached only via the Airtop API/live view, not a dedicated public IPv4 address on the machine

egress_allowlist.quote: The integrated proxy service has a few domains that it cannot access. If you try to access one of these domains, the session will fail.
egress_allowlist.note: Airtop enforces its own fixed proxy exclusion list (streaming, banking, ticketing, LinkedIn); there is no customer-configurable allow/deny egress list or no-internet mode

egress_http_rules.quote: The integrated proxy service has a few domains that it cannot access.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: no HTTP method/path-level egress control is documented

static_egress_ip.quote: Sticky sessions attempt to keep the same IP address for up to 30 minutes at a time. Stickiness is provided on a best-effort basis, as we cannot guarantee that the same IP address will be available for the entire duration.
static_egress_ip.note: Integrated proxy IP is only best-effort sticky for up to 30 minutes, not a fixed/static egress IP; a fully static IP would require a customer-supplied external proxy
